full_judgment: 10. The Court of Settlement took up the application of the petitioners for hearing and the petitioners filed a host of documents. The petitioners also filed a letter written by Khawaja Golam Hossain on 6-1-1981 to the Director of Fire Services asking for his service book and reply of the Director of Fire Services sending the service book with a forwarding letter dated 22-1-1981 to Mr. Khawaja Golam Hossain. The petitioners also filed other documents with a Firisti along with these two documents showing that Khawaja Golam Hossain was an employee of the Fire Services and he was in Bangladesh at least upon 1983 and as such his property cannot be treated as abandoned property. Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW 1. The deposition shows that petitioner No.1 put in the kabalas obtained by the petitioners from Khawaja Golam Hossain. Petitioner No.1 was cross examined, but the genuineness of these kabalas was never questioned and, as such, execution of these kabalas was beyond question and in the absence of any case of these kabalas being forged or fraudulent, respondent-No.1 had no issue before it to question the genuineness of these kabalas. Furthermore, registration of those kabalas carry a presumption of genuineness under section 60 of the Registration Act.
